evidence_policy: Measured on local NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Laptop GPU (sm_86, 16 SMs) under WSL2 /dev/dxg with CUDA 13.1 and Triton 3.9.0.

profiler.note: Uses WP_TIMER=1 (%clock64 + %globaltimer OPEN/CLOSE anchors, ~27 ns step) by default because sm_86 %globaltimer ticks at 1024 ns. Bare-metal Linux uses 200 kHz nsys; WSL2 falls back cleanly to software-only or CUDA-trace window.

entries.construct: cp.async.cg.shared.global -> shared memory (Ampere async tile load)
entries.placement_rule: On sm_86, tl.load / cp.async lowers to non-blocking cp.async.cg.shared.global followed by cp.async.commit_group and cp.async.wait_group before MMA. Use WP_TIMER=1 (%clock64 + OPEN/CLOSE anchors) because %globaltimer has 1024 ns granularity on sm_86.
